claims.text: Elevated-temperature degradation of AM Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 is governed primarily by coupled Al/Cr and Ti oxidation.
Al and Cr rapidly form a thin, initially protective oxide scale during elevated-temperature exposure.
Ti promotes non-stoichiometric, poorly adherent oxide formation at grain boundaries.
The initially protective scale is subsequently undermined by scale spallation and intergranular oxidation.
The degradation mode differs between oxidizing and reducing atmospheres.
The as-built alloy has a homogeneous, fine-grained FCC matrix.
The as-built alloy has high strength and fatigue performance with minimal pre-existing oxidation.
Exposure at about 700 °C in air versus 5% H2 in Ar for 10, 50, and 100 hours provides a controlled atmosphere-and-time comparison.
The relevant structural mediator is the formation, adhesion, and continuity of surface and grain-boundary oxide films, including Al-, Cr-, and Ti-containing oxides.
In air, preferential oxidation of Al and Cr initially retards degradation.
Ti oxidation at grain boundaries generates internal stress that eventually causes scale spallation.
Under 5% H2 in Ar, limited oxygen prevents formation of a continuous protective scale and instead causes dispersed oxides and accelerated intergranular corrosion.
Air-exposed samples will initially develop a continuous mixed Al/Cr-based scale that later becomes disrupted by Ti-rich inclusions and spallation.
Samples exposed to 5% H2 in Ar will show more internal and grain-boundary oxidation and a larger loss of mechanical properties than air-exposed samples.
Observable degradation requires temperatures above approximately 600 °C and exposure durations of at least 10 hours.
Below approximately 600 °C or 10 hours, oxide formation and degradation are negligible.
Oxide chemistry, morphology, continuity, adhesion, grain-boundary penetration, and mechanical-property changes can be measured by SEM, TEM, XPS, hardness, and tensile testing.
The Ti-driven mechanism is falsified if both atmospheres preserve a continuous Al/Cr-rich scale without Ti-rich disruption and produce no significant difference in internal oxidation.
